name: Developer / server
summary: Keep every capability, remove only the junk, then make the phone a machine that can actually hold a service up: no process killer, no doze, stays awake on the charger.
note: The debloat half is deliberately conservative. The valuable part of this profile is the other half: Android spends enormous effort killing long-running background work, and a phone that is serving something needs most of that effort switched off.

standard.label: Standard
standard.blurb: Ads, analytics and paid preloads out. Every tool, store and service stays.

extreme.label: Extreme
extreme.blurb: Also the OEM stores, themes, games hubs and assistants. Anything a developer touches is kept by omission: Chrome, Drive and Docs are tagged 'google' and 'office', and this tier asks for neither, so they are never candidates. A preinstalled Outlook still goes, because it is a paid-for preload rather than a tool you chose.

ultra.label: Ultra
ultra.blurb: A headless server. Everything with a user interface that is not needed to administer the phone goes, including the camera, the gallery and the dialer, and the screen is set never to sleep on the charger.
ultra.warn: Ultra assumes this phone is a server you reach over the network and not a phone you carry. Do not run it on your daily driver.

extra_ops.label: Never sleep while charging (any charger type)
extra_ops.note: Value 7 is AC + USB + wireless. The screen staying on costs power and will age the panel; that is the trade for a machine that never drops off the network.

ops.label: Turn off the phantom process killer
ops.note: Android 12 added a watchdog that kills an app's child processes once it has too many. It is the reason Termux servers die after a few minutes with no error. This is the single most important setting on this list.

ops.label: Stay awake while charging (AC and USB)
ops.note: Keeps the device from dozing on the charger.

ops.label: Exempt Termux from battery optimisation
ops.note: Without this, doze suspends the whole Termux process group whenever the screen has been off for a while and your service stops answering.

server.note: See docs/SERVER.md. The short version: real Docker cannot run on an unrooted phone, because dockerd needs kernel namespaces, cgroups and overlayfs and Android gives an app none of them. Four things do work.

paths.name: Termux + proot-distro
paths.blurb: A Debian userland without containers. Run the service directly. Best for Stirling PDF, nginx, Node and Python apps.

paths.name: udocker
paths.blurb: Runs real OCI images in userspace via PRoot. No isolation and no Compose networking, but `udocker run` works.

paths.name: Android 16 Linux Terminal
paths.blurb: A genuine Debian VM with systemd, where Docker itself runs. Needs protected-VM hardware: Pixels, some Exynos Samsungs, not much else.

paths.name: QEMU VM in Termux
paths.blurb: Real dockerd in an Alpine guest. Works, and is slow enough that you will not enjoy it.
